title: People Ops Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose

This document describes Redwood Inference's standard processes for hiring, new-hire onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and the core manager responsibilities necessary to run an equitable, scalable people program. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and engineering managers.

Scope

- Roles: Individuals contributing to hiring, interviewing, onboarding, performance reviews, and calibration (hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops, hiring partners, managers).
- Systems: Greenhouse (recruiting), Lattice (performance), Rippling (HRIS/payroll), Slack, Google Calendar, Okta (SSO).
- Applicability: Full-time employees, IC contractors on 6+ month engagements, and new managers.

High-level goals and success metrics

- Time-to-fill (requisition opened -> offer accepted): target 35 days.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 80%.
- New-hire ramp-to-productivity (first meaningful contribution): target 60 days; full productivity: target 90 days.
- Interview quality: average interviewer score >= 4.0/5 in interviewer calibration surveys.
- Manager 1:1 frequency: weekly (or biweekly for IC contributors if agreed).

Hiring process (end-to-end)

1. Requisition & Approval
   - Manager files requisition in Greenhouse with role spec, team impact statement, suggested hiring timeline, and budget confirmation.
   - People-ops approves requisition or returns for clarification within 3 business days.

2. Role profile and scorecard (owner: hiring manager + people-ops)
   - Create a concise role profile: mission, success in first 3/6/12 months, required vs. nice-to-have skills, salary band, and interview scorecard.
   - Scorecard sections: technical skill, problem solving, communication, role fit, culture add. Each section has a rubric (0\u20133).

3. Sourcing & Screen
   - Recruiter sources and schedules phone screens; typical sequence: recruiter screen -> hiring manager screen -> technical/role loop -> final round.
   - Recruiter updates Greenhouse stage within 24 hours of interview.

4. Interviewing (interviewer responsibilities)
   - Interviewers must review candidate resume, scorecard, and Greenhouse notes 24 hours before the interview.
   - Use consistent rubrics; avoid asking about protected characteristics.
   - Provide concrete, evidence-backed notes tied to scorecard criteria.
   - Escalate concerns (culture fit or red flags) to the hiring manager and recruiter immediately.

5. Debrief & Decision
   - Hiring manager runs a debrief within 48 hours. Decision options: advance, reject, or request another loop.
   - Offer authority: only people-ops / hiring manager with compensation approval can extend offers. All offers are routed through people-ops for final sign-off and background checks.

6. Offer & Closing
   - Target offer window after final interview: 3 business days.
   - Standard components: base salary, equity, target bonus (if applicable), start date, remote/office expectation, relocation stipend (if applicable).

Interview templates and sample questions

- Recruiter screen (30 min): motivations, role alignment, logistical fit, high-level background.
- Hiring manager screen (30\u201345 min): problem/impact orientation, team fit, top 2\u20133 role-critical questions.
- Technical loop (45\u201360 min): 1\u20132 focused challenges that mirror day-to-day work (no algorithm puzzles unless role requires it).
- Leadership / cross-functional (45 min): stakeholder management, tradeoff decisions, communication examples.

Sample technical prompt (engineering):
- \"Describe a time you optimized inference throughput for a production system. What was your approach, what metrics did you track, and what was the outcome?\"

Scorecard (example columns)

| Criterion | Expectation (0\u20133) | Evidence examples |
|---|---:|---|
| Technical competence | 3 = deep system design for production inference; 0 = no relevant experience | Past project, metrics, code samples |
| Problem solving | 3 = structured approach, measurable impact | Design tradeoffs, metrics |
| Communication | 3 = clear, concise, tailored to audience | Presentation examples, cross-team syncs |
| Role fit | 3 = strong alignment with mission & team workflow | Prior roles & motivations |

Onboarding (first 90 days)

Principles:
- Fast time-to-impact: give new hires a meaningful first project day 1\u201314.
- Psychological safety: early 1:1s and clear success criteria.
- Consistency: use a repeatable checklist to minimize variance.

Preboarding (before Day 1)
- People-ops sends welcome packet with start logistics, first-week schedule, org chart, and IT instructions 7 days before start.
- Manager schedules Day 1 1:1 and assigns a peer buddy.

Day 1\u20137 (orientation and access)
- Complete HR paperwork in Rippling, SSO/Okta setup, Slack access, email, and required security training.
- Intro meetings: manager 30 min 1:1, team 60 min welcome, buddy check-ins, product overview (30 min).
- Deliverable: first-day readme with 3 small tasks and local dev environment checklist.

Week 2\u20134 (first contributions)
- Assign first project with clear objectives and acceptance criteria.
- Weekly manager 1:1 and peer-syncs.
- Lattice goal creation: create 1\u20133 goals tied to team OKRs.
- Feedback checkpoint end of week 4 (manager-led): discuss blockers and ramp plan.

Month 2\u20133 (ownership & feedback)
- Transition from onboarding tasks to ownership of a feature or service.
- 30/60/90 check-ins: structured topics (what went well, blockers, learning goals).
- Manager documents progress in Lattice and shares updates with people-ops for trend analysis.

Onboarding checklist (selected items)

- [ ] HR paperwork completed in Rippling
- [ ] SSO & 2FA configured (Okta)
- [ ] Laptop imaged and access granted
- [ ] Slack & Google Calendar access
- [ ] Local dev environment working
- [ ] First PR merged and reviewed
- [ ] Lattice goals created

Manager responsibilities (summary)

- Hiring: define role, build scorecard, participate in interviews, and drive decisions.
- Onboarding: schedule first-week plan, assign buddy, set 30/60/90 expectations.
- Performance: run regular 1:1s, document feedback in Lattice, prepare for calibration cycles.
- Development: coach for growth, run career conversations quarterly, support promotion readiness.
- Compliance: ensure mandatory trainings completed, verify new-hire paperwork.

Performance & feedback cycles

- Cadence:
  - Continuous feedback: manager to provide actionable notes after significant events (PR feedback, major incidents, presentations).
  - Regular 1:1s: weekly for managers and IC contributors (minimum bi-weekly if agreed).
  - Formal performance reviews: annual baseline + semi-annual calibration for high-growth teams.

- Review stages and timelines (owner: people-ops + managers)
  1. Self-assessment (2 weeks prior to review window).
  2. Manager assessment and written feedback (1 week prior to calibration).
  3. Calibration panels by org lead (HRBP + managers) to normalize scores and promotion decisions.
  4. Calibration outcomes reviewed by People Ops for comp actions.

- Rating scale and criteria (example):
  - Exceeds expectations (E) \u2013 Consistently delivers beyond scope and develops others; ready for stretch promotion readiness evidence.
  - Meets expectations (M) \u2013 Solid delivery at role level with growing autonomy.
  - Needs improvement (N) \u2013 Misses key expectations; needs structured plan.

Promotion & leveling guidance

- Promotion is evidence-based: documented achievements, manager recommendation, peer feedback, and calibration panel approval.
- Promotion packet: updated role expectations, comp recommendation, at least two peer feedback notes, and 30/60/90 future plan.
- Timeline: allow 4\u20136 weeks for packet review and calibration.

Performance improvement plans (PIP)

- When used: for sustained performance gaps after coaching (typically >2 coaching cycles).
- Process: manager builds a time-bound (60\u201390 day) plan with measurable objectives, weekly checkpoints, and HRBP involvement.
- Outcomes: improved performance -> return to normal cycle; insufficient progress -> next steps per policy (role change or separation).

Feedback best practices for managers

- Be timely: give feedback close to events.
- Be specific: cite examples and desired outcomes.
- Balance: emphasize strengths and one area for development.
- Document: note in Lattice and share during 1:1s.

Equity, fairness, and inclusion

- Interview panels must include at least one trained interviewer (interviewer training led by people-ops).
- Structured rubrics reduce noise and bias. Document evidence for hiring and promotion decisions.
- Reasonable accommodations: notify people-ops as soon as candidate/employee requests adjustments.

People policies highlights (manager-facing)

- Time off: managers approve PTO in Rippling. Recommend 2\u20133 weeks notice for planned extended leave.
- Parental leave: up to 16 weeks primary caregiver, 8 weeks secondary caregiver (see full policy in HR portal).
- Remote/office expectations: team-level agreements should be documented; default hybrid expectation is 3 days remote/2 days in-office for non-remote roles unless otherwise approved.
- Probation period: 90 days standard for new hires; managers must complete probation check-in in Lattice before end of day 75.

Tools, templates and quick links

- Greenhouse: requisitions, interview scheduling, offer letters.
- Lattice: goals, 1:1s, performance reviews, calibration reports.
- Rippling: onboarding paperwork, payroll, benefits.
- Interviewer training: link to People Ops training playlist (People Ops > Interviewer Training).

Templates included (copy & adapt)

- Hiring scorecard template (paste into Greenhouse scorecard):
  - Technical (0\u20133):
  - Problem solving (0\u20133):
  - Communication (0\u20133):
  - Team fit (0\u20133):
  - Overall recommendation: Strong Hire / Hire / Borderline / Do Not Hire

- 30/60/90 check-in template (manager-led):
  - 30 days: onboarding progress, blockers, initial wins
  - 60 days: ownership progress, cross-team relationships, development needs
  - 90 days: impact review, goal alignment, promotion readiness (if appropriate)

Escalations & when to involve People Ops

- Offer negotiation beyond band, counteroffers from other employers, complex visa sponsorship questions, performance terminations, and reasonable accommodation requests should be routed to people-ops immediately.

Common FAQs (manager quick answers)

Q: How long should interviews be?
A: Recruiter screens: 30 min. Manager and technical interviews: 45\u201360 min. Salt the loop with short 30 min calls for cross-functional partners if helpful.

Q: When should I start a PIP?
A: After 2+ documented coaching cycles with insufficient improvement. Consult HRBP before issuing a PIP.
